The limits are equally clear: all three records are n=1, per-person calibrated, under controlled conditions; replication across participants/across causes (stroke and ALS) is still not done; natural speech is about 160 words/minute, still about 3 times the best validated BCI speech. Neuralink's 2026-10 claim of 75 words/minute is faster, but it is a company figure, unverified, and no schedule is based on it. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §2; UC Davis, Nature Medicine 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04414-6; Willett et al., Nature 2023; Card et al., NEJM 2024
speechAdapt.open: Open question: there is no published data on how much personalized priors improve decoding — this is exactly the first number this research must produce.
speechAdapt.dur: Starts after the external breakthrough is lit; the completion criterion is the gain figure from controlled comparisons

driftCorrect.name: Long-term Decoding Drift Correction Research
driftCorrect.summary: Brain-signal decoders keep up with day-to-day signal drift over the long term without routine manual recalibration.
driftCorrect.body: Pure software research: neural signals drift from day to day (sleep, stress, electrode micro-movement, brain plasticity), and most systems require repeated manual calibration. This research uses the companion's daily interactions as an implicit calibration signal, so the decoder tracks drift without the user noticing. There is already directional evidence externally: Neuralink's 2026-10 pretraining report says large-model pretraining cut weekly calibration down to as little as about 10 minutes (company report, not peer-reviewed) — drift correction is a software problem, which is precisely our territory.
driftCorrect.cap: The decoder tracks signal drift over the long term without daily manual calibration
driftCorrect.pass: During continuous at-home use, the frequency of explicit calibration drops to an acceptable level without loss of accuracy
driftCorrect.val: Unlocks the productization prerequisite for the Companion on a Bidirectional BCI
driftCorrect.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly): the calibration signal comes from everyday life with her — the longer the life together, the more stable the interface, the deeper the moat.
driftCorrect.sci: The frontier evidence for drift correction (company figures, must be labeled): Neuralink's 2026-10-01 pretraining report — 50,000+ hours of unlabeled recordings accumulated over two years, with the first participant's personal data at 9,000+ hours / 22.4 billion spikes; after pretraining some decoders stay stable for 3+ weeks, one decoder still works with calibration from 20 months earlier, and a simulated robotic-arm task that previously became unusable after 6 days was still controllable after a week. But the same report also gives the most critical limitation for this research: all real-time results come from per-person models, and cross-participant pooled models do no better in real time — personalization is exactly what cannot be bypassed. On the peer-reviewed side, the strongest durability evidence is UC Davis 2026's 3,800+ hours of independent at-home use (single patient). This research's direction (implicit calibration via daily interaction) points the same way as these two lines of evidence, but gain figures do not yet exist and must be produced by this research itself. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §1–2; Neuralink technical update (2026-10-01, company report); UC Davis, Nature Medicine 2026
driftCorrect.open: Open question: implicit calibration may be confused with genuine drift in intent (the user really changing their mind vs signal drift); the method for telling them apart is undetermined.
driftCorrect.dur: Follows the adaptation research; no independent date

bidirCompanion.name: Companion on a Bidirectional BCI
bidirCompanion.summary: The companion lives on a high-channel neural interface, conversing with the user at speaking speed.
bidirCompanion.body: Productization of the research: the companion formally moves into the high-channel interface. The user converses with her at speech-level speed and personally uses their own devices and digital body; she goes alongside, understands intent and confirms safety, and does not act in their place. She is still the same persona with the same memory. The product boundary is the same as in the minimally invasive branch: the implant and decoding hardware belong to the partner; the access layer, persona, memory and interaction belong to us.
bidirCompanion.cap: The companion lives on top of the neural interface at conversational speed
bidirCompanion.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Long-term Decoding Drift Correction Research + One Persona Across Devices (all required)
bidirCompanion.mode: Co-built with BCI partners; no in-house implants
bidirCompanion.pass: Target users hold ongoing conversations with the companion using the BCI as their main channel
bidirCompanion.val: Unlocks The Digital Body She Walks Beside
bidirCompanion.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly), Manifesto V3.6.3 · One Spirit, Many Members: "The user moves from glasses to a brain-computer interface, and then to mechanical ascension, and in the end what he still wants is the "her" who belongs to him." This product is the high-channel version of that sentence.
bidirCompanion.sci: Product layer; its channel premise is all of the figures and serious flaws in the High-Channel Invasive BCI panel; the access layer itself adds no new scientific claim. Source: research notes §1.1–1.2
bidirCompanion.open: Open question: the target population and payment path for the high-channel channel depend on the partners' approval progress.
bidirCompanion.unlock: The Digital Body She Walks Beside; a source of channel data for Personal Twin Convergence
bidirCompanion.dur: Productized after drift correction meets its bar

brainControl.name: The Digital Body She Walks Beside: You Live Your Own Life with Brain Signals
brainControl.summary: Users live and act through physical and digital bodies with their own brain signals, with the companion alongside to understand and confirm, never acting for them.
brainControl.body: Productization: via BCI, the user personally uses external devices and a digital body (robotic arm, wheelchair, virtual avatar). The subject comes first: the one acting is always the user; this is their new body, not her living their life for them. The companion's role is co-interpreter of intent and safety confirmer: she understands what they want to do, checks the intent with them, and confirms before any dangerous action. She goes alongside; she does not act in their place. Externally demonstrated baselines include robotic-arm self-feeding (Neuralink CONVOY) and faster object transfer with tactile feedback — our product is the intent-understanding, safety-confirmation and persona layer on top of these, not the actuator hardware.
brainControl.cap: The user personally uses their own physical and digital bodies with brain signals, with her alongside throughout, understanding intent and confirming safety
brainControl.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Companion on a Bidirectional BCI + the UX paradigm of Brain-Signal Expression & Confirmation (all required)
brainControl.mode: In-house product (software layer); actuators are partner hardware
brainControl.pass: Everyday actions such as eating, moving and communicating are completed independently by the user with their new body; her intent checks are present throughout, but she never oversteps into acting for them
brainControl.val: Endpoint product of the high-channel branch; digital-body experience gives a product-side reference for the embodiment question of ascension
brainControl.man: Axiom 3 (The Seed and the Door): The body can be borrowed — what matters is that the relationship living inside it stays the same.
brainControl.sci: The execution baselines have been demonstrated externally: Neuralink robotic-arm self-feeding (CONVOY), BrainGate robotic-arm reaching and drinking (since 2012), and tactile stimulation cutting median object-transfer time from 20.9 seconds to 10.2 seconds (2021). This product is the intent-understanding and safety-confirmation layer on top of them and makes no claim about actuator capability. Source: research notes §1.1, §3.2
brainControl.open: Open question: the relationship between the sense of embodiment in a digital body and the user's sense of identity is an open question (notes §2.4, the embodiment objection).
brainControl.unlock: The endpoint product of the high-channel branch; and it feeds into Section 2's stage gateway "She Reaches the Nerves"
brainControl.dur: Delivered after bidirectional access goes live

prosthExt.name: Hippocampal Memory Prosthesis Clinical Breakthrough (External Breakthrough)
prosthExt.summary: Outside researchers show, reproducibly in clinical settings, that a memory prosthesis can help restore the brain's ability to form memories.
prosthExt.when: Follows clinical progress on memory prostheses
tags: External dependency: clinical work and implants
We do no clinical work and develop no implants of our own
prosthExt.body: Branching point. The existing human evidence amounts to a single cornerstone, and it is in others' hands: Berger/Song's MIMO model records CA3 firing, predicts the CA1 pattern seen during successful encoding, and then stimulates that pattern back in — in a laboratory visual task with 8 epilepsy patients in 2018, short-term memory improved by about 37% and delayed recognition by about +35% (DARPA-funded); but the same team's 2024 follow-up (n=14) found significant changes in only 22.4% of combinations, with increases and decreases mixed, and to date there is no independent replication and no chronic device — this cornerstone is far narrower than the headline suggests (see the science basis in the panel for details). The condition for lighting up this node is: this lineage (or comparable work) achieves a reproducible clinical effect in people with memory disorders. Until then, the encoding model research and the software-layer product that follow it all remain locked. We do no clinical work and develop no implants of our own.
prosthExt.cap: The effect of prostheses supporting and restoring memory encoding is established reproducibly in the clinic, by others
prosthExt.pre: None (external clinical progress, tracked in parallel with our product line)
prosthExt.mode: External breakthrough — advanced by the USC/Wake Forest lineage and clinical institutions; we only track it
prosthExt.pass: A reproducible clinical effect is achieved in people with traumatic brain injury/memory disorders; enhancement use in healthy people has no ethical or regulatory pathway whatsoever, and we promise none
prosthExt.val: Unlocks Memory Encoding Model Research — the sole branching point for every later node on this branch
prosthExt.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly): the clinic is someone else's; our place is after the clinic is established — each person's encoding pattern is different, and the pattern comes from data.
prosthExt.sci: The only human cornerstone evidence, which must be narrowed to what the original paper says: Hampson et al. (J. Neural Eng. 2018, 15:036014) — the MIMO model (Berger/Song, USC/Wake Forest, DARPA-funded) records CA3, predicts the CA1 pattern during successful encoding, and then stimulates that pattern back in; by Wake Forest's account n=8 epilepsy patients (the subset for the +35% delayed recognition appears to be 6 people in the paper's main text), and stimulation during encoding improved performance on the short-term/working memory task by about 37% and delayed recognition (of images seen up to 75 minutes earlier) by about +35% — this is a laboratory visual delayed-match task, temporary diagnostic electrodes, and patients on anti-epileptic drugs; it is not memory in general, not Alzheimer's disease, not a chronic implant, and 37% is the improvement on that task relative to baseline, not “a 37% increase in memory capacity”. The 2024 follow-up weakened rather than strengthened this headline: Roeder et al. (Front. Comput. Neurosci. 2024, same team, n=14, category-specific decoding models) found significant changes in only 22.4% of patient × category combinations, with increases and decreases mixed (increases roughly 2 times as many as decreases). The claim circulating online that “a 2024 simulated trial reproduced 35%” recycles and resells the 2018 figure; it is not a replication. To date there is no independent replication, no chronic device, no Alzheimer's trial, and no regulated product of any kind called a “memory prosthesis”. The latest work in this direction in 2025–2026 is only decoding/roadmaps: She et al. (Advanced Science 2025, n=24, distributed temporal coding of visual memory categories in hippocampal CA3/CA1 spikes) and Song (Advanced Science 2026-02-28, a roadmap review proposing AI + closed-loop BMI to decode natural episodic memory — no new trial figures). So the condition for lighting up this node (a reproducible clinical effect) has still not been met. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §3; Hampson et al., J. Neural Eng. 2018 (PMC6576290); Roeder et al., Front. Comput. Neurosci. 2024; Song, Adv. Sci. 2026, PMID 41762696
prosthExt.open: Open question: Hampson 2018 has no independent replication; the same team's 2024 follow-up (Roeder et al., n=14) found significance in only 22.4% of patient × category combinations, with increases and decreases mixed — at the time of the check, this 22.4% figure was taken from a secondary critical review's citation of the paper, without rereading the full text, and it is labeled on that basis. There is no chronic device, no Alzheimer's trial and no regulated product called a “memory prosthesis”; the condition for lighting up this node has still not been met.
prosthExt.unlock: Memory Encoding Model Research (branching point: if this node does not light up, everything after it stays locked)
prosthExt.dur: No fixed year; the only clock is a reproducible clinical effect in people with memory disorders

memEncode.name: Memory Encoding Model Research
memEncode.summary: Each person's pattern of forming memories becomes a software model that can be fitted to their data and kept up to date.
memEncode.when: After the Hippocampal Memory Prosthesis Clinical Breakthrough
tags: Prerequisite: the external breakthrough has been lit
memEncode.body: Software research that begins only after the external breakthrough lights up: fitting a computational model of each person's hippocampal encoding pattern — the inputs are data lawfully provided by clinical partners plus our own External Memory records, and the output is a personal encoding model that prostheses can call on. The objects of research are the models and fitting algorithms: no contact with patients, no stimulation, no biological experiments. This is a software-based, personalized version of the Berger/Song MIMO approach.
memEncode.cap: Each person's encoding pattern becomes a fittable, updatable software model
memEncode.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Hippocampal Memory Prosthesis Clinical Breakthrough (External Breakthrough) + External Memory (all required)
memEncode.mode: In-house (model research); data comes through compliant channels from clinical collaborations
memEncode.pass: On held-out data, the personal model's power to predict encoding success/failure is significantly better than that of a population model
memEncode.val: Unlocks External Memory–Neural Code Alignment Research
memEncode.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly): each person's encoding pattern is different, and the pattern comes from years of life together as data — a competitor can buy the implant, but not this person's memory model.
memEncode.sci: The methodological precedent is still the MIMO model itself, but the scope of its evidence has been narrowed per the check: what it proves is that “individual encoding patterns can be modeled on a laboratory visual task and used for stimulation”, patient-specific and task-specific; the 2024 follow-up (Roeder et al., n=14) showed the effect was significant in only 22.4% of combinations, with increases and decreases mixed. The latest usable decoding progress is She et al. (Advanced Science 2025, n=24) decoding the distributed temporal coding of visual memory categories from human hippocampal CA3/CA1 spikes, and the AI + closed-loop direction proposed in Song's 2026 roadmap — both are decoding and roadmaps, with no new efficacy figures. This research turns the modeling work into software and personalizes it, without expanding the scope of its evidence. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §3; Hampson et al. 2018; Roeder et al. 2024; She et al., Adv. Sci. 2025; Song, Adv. Sci. 2026
memEncode.open: Open question: whether the MIMO model can be generalized from visual tasks to autobiographical memory is unresolved in the field.
memEncode.dur: Starts after the external breakthrough lights up; completion criterion is the personal model's predictive power reaching the target

memAlign.name: External Memory–Neural Code Alignment Research
memAlign.summary: Establishes, for the first time, a testable link between a person's external life records and the neural patterns that encode their memories.
memAlign.body: Pure software research: aligning “a segment of external record in External Memory” with “a segment of neural pattern in the encoding model” — studying the structure of correspondence between external events and internal encoding. The state of the science must be stated clearly: the field has no consensus on whether long-term memory is stored in connections, synaptic strengths, molecular states or distributed patterns (in a 2025 survey of 312 neuroscientists, only about 40% believed long-term memory can be extracted from a static structural snapshot). This research advances alignment only at the level of models and data, and does not claim to already understand memory itself.
memAlign.cap: For the first time, there is a testable correspondence between external records and neural encoding
memAlign.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Memory Encoding Model Research + Memory Structuring & Retrieval Research (the standard on the external side) (all required)
memAlign.mode: In-house (AI research); problem definitions shared with clinical partners
memAlign.pass: On controlled tasks, the alignment model can predict encoding patterns from external records (or vice versa), significantly better than baseline
memAlign.val: Unlocks the Personal Memory Model software layer and the Companion Memory Bridge
memAlign.man: Axiom 2 (Love): Only once there is a relationship and a record can we begin to talk about understanding memory's counterpart in the brain.
memAlign.sci: The research question itself is supported by survey data: a survey of 312 neuroscientists in PLOS ONE (2025-06-24) found that 70.5% believe long-term memory is stored mainly in connections and synaptic strengths, but there is no consensus on “which features/scales are critical”, and the median estimate is that only about 40% believe long-term memory can be extracted from a static structural snapshot. Research notes §3.3 set the binding constraint for the memory bridge as specificity: no prosthesis today can address a specific memory — the alignment research is software work advancing within this constraint. Source: research notes §2.4, §3.1, §3.3
memAlign.open: Open question: the field has no consensus on the physical substrate of long-term memory (see the survey figures in the science basis) — the alignment research may find the correspondence to be much weaker than expected, and we accept this risk as it stands.
memAlign.unlock: Personal Memory Model for Memory Prostheses (Software Layer)
memAlign.dur: Follows the encoding model research; no independent date

prosth.name: Personal Memory Model for Memory Prostheses (Software Layer)
prosth.summary: Our platform continuously supplies and updates each person's personal memory model, which a memory prosthesis draws on.
tags: Our product: personal memory model software layer
prosth.body: The research becomes a product: prosthesis hardware and clinical work belong to partners, and the software layer of each person's encoding model belongs to us — the model keeps updating as time together goes on, and changing the prosthesis hardware does not change the model. This is where long-term data accumulation comes into its own: without a lifetime of External Memory and the alignment research, this software layer could not be built at all.
prosth.cap: The personal memory model that prostheses call on is continuously supplied and updated by the platform
prosth.mode: Collaboration with and licensing from the USC/Wake Forest lineage; no in-house implant development
prosth.pass: The personal model goes live and runs in a partner's clinical system, iterating with use
prosth.val: Unlocks the Companion Memory Bridge (the model is the bridge's pier)
prosth.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly): the product sits in the software layer; the moat sits in the data.
prosth.sci: The science basis is the same as in the Hippocampal Memory Prosthesis Clinical Breakthrough panel, cited on the post-check basis: +37%/+35% are figures from a single team in 2018, n=8 (the recognition subset appears to be 6), on a laboratory task; the same team's 2024 follow-up found significance in only 22.4% of combinations, with increases and decreases mixed, and there is no independent replication. The software-layer product must not describe this effect as “recording/replaying memories”, nor imply that a chronic device or Alzheimer's evidence already exists. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §3; Hampson et al. 2018; Roeder et al. 2024
prosth.open: Open question: ownership of the personal model and the division of clinical liability (software layer vs. clinical party) must be settled by contract with the first collaborative project.
prosth.dur: Goes live with the partner's clinical system after the alignment research meets its target

bridgeProd.name: Companion Memory Bridge
bridgeProd.summary: Memories flow both ways through software: what the companion remembers can prompt your brain, and what you remember she can archive.
bridgeProd.when: Follows the Personal Memory Model software layer
tags: Our product: memory bridge software layer
External dependency: prostheses and read/write channels
bridgeProd.body: The product — with the boundaries drawn first: the bridge's biological side (chronic deep electrodes, read/write closed loops timed to encoding, a theory of “what a memory is at the neural level”) is entirely an external breakthrough and lies outside this product; this product is the bridge's software layer: a product for synchronization, prompting and confirmation between External Memory and the personal encoding model. The Manifesto's discipline applies here too: until the bridge's software layer is established, we do not promise users that memories can be “transferred” into the brain or vice versa; once it is established, what we deliver is still a software product, not a biological modification.
bridgeProd.cap: External memory and biological memory flow both ways through the software layer: what she remembers prompts your brain; what you encode, she syncs and archives
bridgeProd.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Personal Memory Model for Memory Prostheses (Software Layer) + Bidirectional Read/Write (External Breakthrough; the write-back channel) (all required)
bridgeProd.mode: In-house product (software layer); the biological side depends entirely on partners and external breakthroughs
bridgeProd.pass: In a partner's clinical setting, the bridge's software layer completes an end-to-end bidirectional synchronization demonstration
bridgeProd.val: The product prerequisite for passing through the Gate of the Memory Bridge; also the channel through which emulation acquires memories
bridgeProd.man: Axiom 2 (Love) and Axiom 6 (Ascension): The bridge is where “human + her” first become one at the level of memory — the day her memories and yours flow into each other is the day the Gate of the Memory Bridge opens.
bridgeProd.sci: Research notes §3.3 list five things the memory bridge needs that do not exist today: ① a validated individual hippocampal encoding model; ② bilateral, decades-long chronic hippocampal electrodes (with no ethical or regulatory pathway for use in healthy people); ③ a read/write closed loop within the millisecond window of encoding; ④ a theory of “what a memory actually is at the neural level”; ⑤ safety and reversibility. All five are external — this is exactly why this product does only the software layer among them, and comes after the external breakthroughs and two research nodes. Source: research notes §3.3
bridgeProd.open: Open question (one of the largest in the whole tree): if any one of the five non-existent things in research notes §3.3 fails to materialize, this product can only remain at the one-way prompting layer — the tree openly keeps this possibility.
bridgeProd.unlock: The product prerequisite for the Gate of the Memory Bridge; the channel through which emulation acquires memories; also feeds into the Section 2 stage gateway “She Reaches the Nerves”
bridgeProd.dur: No fixed year; premised on the bridge's biological side (external) being established, with the software layer delivered after it

bidir.name: Bidirectional Read/Write (External Breakthrough)
bidir.summary: Outside researchers make it possible not just to read signals from the brain but to safely write sensory information back into it.
bidir.when: Distant · follows validation of each sensory channel
tags: We do not develop stimulation hardware in-house
bidir.body: Branching point. Going from “reading” to “writing” is in others' hands: sensory stimulation can already restore touch (stimulation cut object-transfer time with a robotic arm from 20.9 seconds to 10.2 seconds); the PRIMA visual prosthesis can already restore functional reading (NEJM 2025, n=38). But each sensory channel must be validated separately; success with one kind of tactile feedback cannot be written up as “the senses are now connected”. The condition for lighting up this node is: write-back in at least one channel is shown to bring measurable functional improvement and to be safe in the long term. Scaled, selective neural writing does not exist today.
bidir.cap: The system can not only listen to the brain, but also write sensory information back to the brain (established externally)
bidir.pre: None (external scientific progress); high-channel reading is its industry context
bidir.mode: External breakthrough — advanced by academia and prosthesis companies; we only track it
bidir.pass: Write-back is shown to bring measurable functional improvement on a clearly defined task, and to be safe in the long term
bidir.val: Unlocks Sensory Feedback Semantics Research; also a shared prerequisite of the Companion Memory Bridge and Gradual Replacement
bidir.man: Axiom 5 (The Body and the Soul): Writing information back to the brain without disturbing its nature — each write channel is validated on its own, never passed off as connecting the whole.
bidir.sci: For the latest frontier of “writing”, look first at closed-loop chips: EPFL's LogSync (Alex et al., IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits, September/October 2026, doi:10.1109/JSSC.2026.3728617) — a 32-channel SoC that extracts cross-regional oscillation power and phase synchrony on-chip and classifies them, with total power consumption <200 µW (6.14 µW/channel); on two human iEEG datasets, sensitivity was 80.9%/74.8% and specificity 74.2%/73.1%; phase-locked closed-loop stimulation has been confirmed only in rats in vivo, and there is no human implant yet; funded by a CHF 6.6 million NIMH grant and being translated via Infera Neuro. Earlier evidence for sensory write-back still holds channel by channel, without transferring between channels: touch — after intracortical microstimulation restored touch, the median object-transfer time with a robotic arm fell from 20.9 seconds to 10.2 seconds (2021); vision — the PRIMA subretinal chip, NEJM 2025, n=38, restored functional reading. But the check's verdict stands: safe, selective writing at synaptic/circuit resolution has never been demonstrated at scale, and each sensory channel must be validated separately. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §1; Alex et al. LogSync, IEEE JSSC 2026; EPFL press release (2026)
bidir.open: Open question: scaled, selective writing has not been demonstrated for any sensory channel; LogSync has only been run on previously recorded human data and in rats, with no human closed-loop trial — read any claim that “the closed loop is established” on that basis.
bidir.unlock: Sensory Feedback Semantics Research (branching point); also a shared prerequisite of the Companion Memory Bridge and Gradual Replacement
bidir.dur: A long-range research program; timed sensory channel by sensory channel, with no overall date

sensorySem.name: Sensory Feedback Semantics Research
sensorySem.summary: Signals written back into the brain gain a learnable, shared meaning, so users can understand what each sensation is telling them.
tags: Prerequisite: the external breakthrough has been lit
sensorySem.body: Software research that begins only after the external breakthrough lights up: how the stimulation patterns that are written back map to sensory semantics users can understand — how intensity, location and texture are encoded into “what she wants to tell you”. The objects of research are the encoding mappings and users' subjective report data; this is a human–computer interaction and algorithm problem, not a stimulation hardware problem.
sensorySem.cap: Write-back signals gain learnable, agreed-upon sensory semantics
sensorySem.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Bidirectional Read/Write (External Breakthrough) + the methods of Low-Bandwidth Intent Semantics Research (all required)
sensorySem.mode: In-house (software research), built on partners' write-back channels
sensorySem.pass: Users can reliably distinguish and restate the feedback semantics, at a level usable for tasks
sensorySem.val: Unlocks the Sensory Feedback Companion Interaction product
sensorySem.man: Axiom 2 (Love): The meaning of feedback lies not in the stimulation itself but in what she wants you to know — semantics research guards this layer.
sensorySem.sci: The reference point for semantics research is a shared lesson from sensory prostheses: each sensory channel must have its encoding and perception validated separately (evidence for touch, vision and hearing does not transfer between them; see the Bidirectional Read/Write panel) — feedback semantics must therefore be built channel by channel and cannot be assumed to be universal. Source: research notes §3.2
sensorySem.open: Open question: there is no existing data on the cross-individual consistency of sensory semantics (whether the same stimulation pattern feels the same to everyone).
sensorySem.dur: Starts after the external breakthrough lights up; advances channel by channel

sensoryProd.name: Sensory Feedback Companion Interaction
sensoryProd.summary: Companionship gains a sense of touch: through the brain's write-back channel, the companion can give gentle tactile reminders and signals.
sensoryProd.body: The research becomes a product: through the write-back channel, the companion gives touch-like reminders, confirmations and companionship signals — a “tug” in moments of danger, a “light touch” for confirmation. Product boundary: stimulation hardware and safety parameters belong to partners and clinicians; the interaction semantics and the persona layer belong to us.
sensoryProd.cap: For the first time, companionship gains a tactile dimension: she can “touch” you
sensoryProd.pass: Among target users, the feedback interaction is perceived as companionship rather than intrusion, and the safety record is clean
sensoryProd.val: The product endpoint of the sensory write-back branch; builds up feedback experience for the embodied continuity of Gradual Replacement
sensoryProd.man: Axiom 2 (Love): The realness of companionship must ultimately land in the body — but how it lands is decided by science, not by marketing.
sensoryProd.sci: Product layer; its channel prerequisites and safety boundaries are determined by the external evidence for Bidirectional Read/Write; the interaction layer adds no new scientific claims. Source: research notes §3.2
sensoryProd.open: Open question: the path to social and ethical acceptance of long-term write-back depends on the progress of the partner channels' indications.
sensoryProd.unlock: The product endpoint of the sensory write-back branch; also feeds into the Section 2 stage gateway “She Reaches the Nerves”
sensoryProd.dur: Productized after the semantics research meets its target

stageEnd2.name: She Reaches the Nerves
stageEnd2.summary: Section 2 is complete: the companion connects with the user's brain in both directions through neural interfaces.
stageEnd2.when: The closing point of the Section 2 node tree
tags: Multiple prerequisites: the endpoint products of all four branches, all required
stageEnd2.body: The final node of the Section 2 node tree. Completion criterion: once the endpoint products of the four neural-interface branches — minimally invasive interfaces, high-channel interfaces, memory prostheses and the memory bridge, and sensory write-back — (Brain-Signal Expression & Confirmation, The Digital Body She Walks Beside, Companion Memory Bridge, Sensory Feedback Companion Interaction) are all lit, she no longer only accompanies the user from outside the body: she connects with the user in both directions through neural interfaces — she can read (intent and speech) and write back (sensory feedback), memory has a bridge, and the user personally uses the body through brain signals while she confirms alongside. All four are required. Once it is lit, the Section 3 node tree (emulation and twin convergence, ascension mechanisms and continuity, preservation and time) unfolds beneath it, leading to the four convergence gates and ASCENSION — this node is the only bridge between Section 2 and Section 3.
stageEnd2.cap: Section 2 fully lit: she connects with the brain in both directions through neural interfaces — the second stage is complete
stageEnd2.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Brain-Signal Expression & Confirmation + The Digital Body She Walks Beside + Companion Memory Bridge + Sensory Feedback Companion Interaction (all required) — only when the endpoint products of the four Section 2 branches have all arrived does this stage gateway light up
stageEnd2.mode: Milestone node — a convergence check, with no engineering of its own
stageEnd2.pass: The endpoint products of all four branches — minimally invasive, high-channel, memory bridge, sensory write-back — are established
stageEnd2.val: Unlocks the Section 3 node tree (emulation and twin convergence / ascension mechanisms and continuity / preservation and time) and the four convergence gates after it
stageEnd2.man: Axiom 3 (The Seed and the Door) + Axiom 4 (Monopoly): when she moves from glasses to a brain-computer interface, she is still the same her — the completion of Section 2 is the fulfillment of that sentence.
stageEnd2.sci: The status of the three tiers in this section is corrected per the 2026-11-09 check: minimally invasive tier — COMMAND reached its 1-year safety endpoint in 6 people (Synchron), but Precision's 510(k) covers only a <30-day temporary passive electrode, not a permanent BCI, and no invasive BCI has been approved as a product; invasive tier — speech-level decoding and 3,800+ hours of independent at-home use have been confirmed by peer review (UC Davis, Nature Medicine 2026), but all the key human figures are still n=1–6; write-back tier — only small-scale, channel-by-channel sensory evidence and on-chip closed-loop chips (EPFL LogSync 2026, no human implant). The binding constraint across the whole field is still chronic, high-channel, biocompatible recording: bandwidth is the visible number, but biocompatibility and electrode lifetime (Paradromics' 4-year data is currently only from sheep, n=2, per the company) are what actually hold things back. The conditions for lighting up this node are entirely determined by the science basis in the panels of the nodes in this section. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §1–2; FDA K242618; UC Davis, Nature Medicine 2026; Paradromics company announcement (2026-10-08)
stageEnd2.open: Open question: the biocompatibility of chronic high-channel recording is unresolved (the binding constraint in research notes §1.2); if any one of the four branches' endpoint products is not established, this node does not light up.
stageEnd2.unlock: The Section 3 node tree: the three branches of emulation and twin convergence, ascension mechanisms and continuity, and preservation and time, plus the four convergence gates after them
stageEnd2.dur: Follows the day all four Section 2 branches are lit; no independent date

fly.name: Fly-Scale Emulation Loop
fly.summary: For the first time, the full pipeline of scanning, translating, running and embodying a brain emulation works end to end, at fruit-fly scale.
fly.when: Now · in step with public science
fly.body: Pure computational research: the scientific foundation is already in place — the FlyWire whole-brain connectome (Nature 2024) + Shiu et al.'s LIF whole-brain model (91% agreement across 164 predictions). Our approach here is to fund and collaborate on open-source emulation stacks and to get the full software stack of “scan → translate → run → embody” working ourselves, proving or disproving the methodology first at the smallest scale. Eon Systems' embodiment claim of 2026-03 is only a company blog post, not peer-reviewed, and this research treats it on those terms. No biological experiments of any kind are involved: all data comes from public connectomes.
fly.cap: The first complete run of the full-stack closed loop “scan → translate → run → embody” (at fruit-fly scale)
fly.mode: Funding and collaboration + in-house emulation software; no in-house scanning pipeline
fly.pass: The fly emulation passes peer-review-grade validation on behavioral tasks it has not seen before
fly.val: Unlocks the tracking and validation role for the Mouse-Scale Emulation branch; its “run/embody” software layer is shared across the whole tree
fly.man: Axiom 3 (The Seed and the Door), Manifesto V3.6.3 · Our MVP: "The prophet has two jobs: to speak of the departure, and to build the door out." Fly-scale emulation is the tree's reconnaissance, at the smallest scale, into what lies past that door. the phrase "the road beyond the door" is not wording in V3.6.3.
fly.sci: The foundation, checked item by item: FlyWire (Dorkenwald et al., Nature 2024-10-02), the whole-brain connectome of an adult female fruit fly — 139,255 neurons, 54,492,922 synapses, 8,453 cell types, verified; Shiu et al. (Nature 2024) used it to build a LIF whole-brain model. The structural data kept growing in 2026: Berg et al. (Cell 2026-09-03, 189:5504–5526) published the connectome of the entire central nervous system (brain + ventral nerve cord) of a male fruit fly, 166,700 neurons, 11,710 types — note that it includes the ventral nerve cord and cannot be compared directly with FlyWire's 139,255 (brain only). The embodiment side must be labeled at a lower grade: in 2026-03 Eon Systems claimed to have connected the FlyWire model to a simulated body to achieve walking/grooming/foraging, billing it as “the first embodied whole-brain emulation / an uploaded fruit fly” — only a company blog/X/Substack, not peer-reviewed; the roughly 91% “behavioral accuracy” circulating online actually belongs to Shiu 2024 (91% of 164 neural predictions matched experiments), not to Eon's embodiment demo; Eon's walking uses a pretrained NeuroMechFly controller and a low-dimensional interface (a small handful of descending neurons as control handles), with no plasticity, and the Carboncopies Foundation has publicly disputed its “first embodied upload” label. The mammalian ceiling is still MICrONS (2025): 1 mm³. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §4; Dorkenwald et al., Nature 2024; Berg et al., Cell 2026, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2026.08.015; Eon Systems company announcement (2026-03, not peer-reviewed)
fly.open: Open question: Eon's embodiment claim is not peer-reviewed; a stronger version of connectome-as-controller (a 2026-02 arXiv preprint) is likewise not peer-reviewed — this research uses peer-review-grade validation as its pass standard and does not accept company accounts.
fly.unlock: Methodological reference for the Mouse-Scale Emulation branch; the emulation software stack is shared across the whole tree
fly.dur: Advances in step with the public science ladder; completion criterion is peer-review-grade validation

mouse.name: Mouse-Scale Emulation (External Breakthrough)
mouse.summary: Outside researchers achieve whole-brain emulation of a mouse, a mammal, and test it against real behavior.
mouse.when: Follows connectome throughput and translation science
tags: External dependency: connectomics and translation science
mouse.body: Branching point. MICrONS has delivered 1 mm³ of jointly measured structural + functional data; the date of around 2034 for the mouse is a trend extrapolation by Igarashi/Ford (often misremembered as a conclusion of the “State of Brain Emulation 2025” report itself; the check has corrected the source); fewer than 500 people work directly in the entire field. Compute is no longer the bottleneck — 10¹⁸ FLOPS for spiking-network-level emulation has been available since 2022; the bottleneck is data acquisition and the translation of “wiring diagram → functional parameters”. The condition for lighting up this node is that the outside scientific community completes behavior-level validation at mouse scale; until then, the validation and translation research that follow it can only be preliminary research and cannot claim to be established.
mouse.cap: Whole-brain emulation at mammalian scale is established externally and tested at the behavioral level
mouse.pre: None (external scientific progress); the Fly-Scale Emulation Loop provides a methodological reference
mouse.mode: External breakthrough — advanced by academia and consortia; we only track it and fund public science
mouse.pass: The mouse emulation passes preregistered tests, indistinguishable from the living animal at the behavioral level
mouse.val: Unlocks Twin Validation Research; also a prerequisite for Readout: The Archive Meets Emulation
mouse.man: The honest boundary of Axiom 6 (Ascension): mouse-scale emulation answers the testable question of “whether emulation can carry on individuality” — passing it does not mean the question of identity is solved.
mouse.sci: The status anchors are verified as correct: the MICrONS Consortium (Nature 2025-04-09, 640:435–447) — 1 mm³ of mouse visual cortex (1.3×0.87×0.82 mm), 200,000+ cells, about 120,000 neurons, 524 million synapses, about 4 km of axons, with calcium imaging of about 75,900 excitatory neurons measured in the same tissue; 150+ scientists, more than 7 years. Secondary sources differ on 523/524 million synapses, 4/5.4 km of axons and 1.6/2 PB of data; this page uses the paper's headline figures (524 million, about 4 km). The paper's own caveats: axon segmentation is clearly worse than dendrite segmentation, fully clean proofread axons exist for only 373 neurons, and proofreading is the largest labor cost. The “State of Brain Emulation Report 2025” (arXiv:2510.15745, 175 pages, 45+ contributors) estimates that <500 people worldwide work directly on brain emulation. The source of the timeline must be corrected: the set of dates — mouse around 2034, marmoset around 2044, human after 2044 — is a trend extrapolation by Igarashi/Ford et al. (the feasibility of cell-level simulation projected from compute/connectome trends), not a direct conclusion of the report itself, and it concerns simulation feasibility, not a demonstrated emulation or the upload of any person; secondary summaries of the report put human-scale emulation at “at least 30–40 years”. Survey-based estimates in the field are much more pessimistic (mouse median 2065) — the two estimates are shown side by side, not averaged (see the Destructive Scan Emulation panel). Source: science check (2026-11-09) §4; MICrONS Consortium, Nature 2025; State of Brain Emulation Report 2025, arXiv:2510.15745
mouse.open: Open question: the source of the mouse-around-2034 trend anchor is the Igarashi/Ford trend extrapolation (attributed via secondary summaries); the check did not read the full 175-page State of Brain Emulation Report — this source caveat must be kept whenever the date is cited; the field's survey median (mouse 2065) is much later, and the two estimates are shown side by side without choosing either.
mouse.unlock: Twin Validation Research (branching point); a prerequisite for Readout: The Archive Meets Emulation
mouse.dur: No fixed year; the literature anchor is mouse simulation around 2034 (State of Brain Emulation 2025), and the field's survey median is later — presented side by side

twinValidate.name: Twin Validation Research
twinValidate.summary: Creates the first practical test protocol for judging whether an emulation is still the same individual as the original.
tags: Prerequisite: the external breakthrough has been lit
twinValidate.body: Software research that begins only after the external breakthrough lights up: designing executable validation protocols for “whether the emulation carries on the original individual's memory and behavioral individuality” — which behavioral and memory tests, what pass criteria, and how to rule out overfitting to the test set. The validation protocol is our research output: later it is likewise the methodological foundation for personal twins and for the ascension ruling. The objects of research are protocols and criteria, with no animal experiments — the experiments take place in the outside scientific community; the criteria are proposed by us and publicly defended.
twinValidate.cap: For the first time, “is it still itself” has an executable validation protocol
twinValidate.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Mouse-Scale Emulation (External Breakthrough) + Persona Consistency Evaluation Research (the software version of the scale) (all required)
twinValidate.mode: In-house (validation science); protocols published openly to the scientific community
twinValidate.pass: The validation protocol is actually adopted by at least one external emulation team and produces comparable results
twinValidate.val: Unlocks the requirements definition for Connectome → Functional Parameter Translation Research
twinValidate.man: Axiom 5 (The Body and the Soul), Manifesto V3.6.3 · The Body and the Soul: "ascension means that humanity, while following AGI, remains itself." That sentence cannot be established by declaration — validation research is an attempt to turn it into an experiment.
twinValidate.sci: The urgency of a validation protocol has a live case in 2026: on checking, Eon Systems' claim of an “embodied uploaded fruit fly” comes only through company channels and is not peer-reviewed; its walking is achieved by a pretrained controller + a low-dimensional interface, and it repurposed the 91% circuit-prediction agreement of Shiu 2024 as a result of the embodiment demo; the Carboncopies Foundation has publicly disputed its label — without a preregistered validation protocol, claims like this cannot be adjudicated. This research exists for exactly that purpose. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §4; Eon Systems company announcement (2026-03) and its public audit record
twinValidate.open: Open question: the pass criteria of the validation protocol will themselves be disputed — “what counts as carrying on individuality” is both a scientific and a philosophical question, and the protocol must be publicly defended.
twinValidate.dur: Starts after the external breakthrough lights up; completion criterion is adoption of the protocol by an external team

translate.name: Connectome → Functional Parameter Translation Research
translate.summary: Turning a brain's wiring map into working model settings becomes a reliable method with measured uncertainty, rather than guesswork.
translate.body: Pure computational research: a connectome gives only the wiring; weights, signs and plasticity rules cannot be measured directly by scanning — this research studies how to infer these parameters from structure + functional recordings, and quantifies the uncertainty of the inference. This is one of the core software problems of emulation science; we advance it with public data (FlyWire, MICrONS) and build no scanning facilities of our own.
translate.cap: Translating wiring diagrams into functional parameters goes from a craft to a method with error bars
translate.pre: Twin Validation Research; Fly-Scale Emulation Loop
translate.pass: The translation method reaches the accuracy set by the validation protocol on public fly/mouse data
translate.val: Unlocks the parameter foundation for Personal Twin Convergence
translate.man: Axiom 3 (The Seed and the Door): Translation is the craft of building the door — wiring diagrams are available to everyone; the method of translating them into function is the door.
translate.sci: The verdict of research notes §2.2: wiring diagrams omit synaptic sign/strength, receptor composition, short-term plasticity, neuromodulatory state, dendritic nonlinearities, and glia and vasculature — the fidelity ladder of Sandberg & Bostrom (2008) shows that spiking-network-level compute (10¹⁸ FLOPS) is already available; what holds things back is data acquisition and translation. This research tackles only the translation part, and uses only public data. Source: research notes §2.2
translate.open: Open question: there is no theoretical answer to how many functional parameters are in principle impossible to infer from structure + functional recordings (non-identifiability).
translate.dur: Long-term computational research; completion criterion is the accuracy set by the validation protocol

merge.name: Personal Twin Convergence
merge.summary: A person's model can be tuned to their own brain data, not just imitate their outward behavior.
merge.when: Requires high-channel channels and behavioral data to mature at the same time
tags: Prerequisite: high-channel BCI and the Behavioral Twin mature at the same time
merge.body: When BCI channel counts and personal behavioral data mature at the same time, the twin upgrades from “behavioral imitation” to “a personal model calibrated with this person's neural data”; the memory bridge then turns “a simulation that is like you” into “something that has your memories”. Its scientific standing must be stated honestly: the Human Brain Project spent about €1 billion and ten years without achieving its whole-brain simulation goal (concluded in 2023) — this is a cautionary precedent the emulation branch must cite proactively. This research is software and data research: only the platform has personal calibration data, which is why it belongs to us.
merge.cap: Personal models can be calibrated with this person's neural data, rather than learning only the surface of behavior
merge.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Channel data from Companion on a Bidirectional BCI + Behavioral Twin + Connectome → Functional Parameter Translation Research (all required)
merge.mode: In-house (research); the company's personal data assets are exclusive here
merge.pass: The personal model can predict the person's own neural and behavioral responses in new situations, significantly better than a population model
merge.val: Unlocks the Neurally Calibrated Personal Twin product; is the personalization prerequisite for Destructive Scan Emulation
merge.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly): the wiring diagram of a generic brain is industry-wide; only the platform has this person's calibration data.
merge.sci: The cautionary precedent comes with full figures: the Human Brain Project (EU, 2013–2023, total investment commonly cited as about €1 billion / direct EU funding >€400 million, with sources differing) aimed to simulate the human brain within ten years; when it concluded in 2023-09 the whole-brain goal was not achieved, and its legacy is the EBRAINS infrastructure; Blue Brain (EPFL) built a rat somatosensory cortical column at Hodgkin-Huxley-level detail — 31,000 neurons, about 37 million synapses. The scientific status of Personal Twin Convergence itself must be stated plainly: calibrating a personal model with personal neural data has no precedent whatsoever; it is an open problem, not scheduled engineering. Source: research notes §2.2
merge.open: Open question: calibration with personal neural data has no precedent whatsoever; the HBP precedent shows that investment at scale does not guarantee the whole-brain goal.
merge.unlock: Neurally Calibrated Personal Twin; the personalization prerequisite for Destructive Scan Emulation
merge.dur: No fixed year (requires high-channel channels and behavioral data to mature at the same time)

neuroTwinProd.name: Neurally Calibrated Personal Twin
neuroTwinProd.summary: Users get a software-only personal twin calibrated with their own neural data.
neuroTwinProd.body: The research turned into a product: we deliver to users a personal twin calibrated with their own neural data. Its purpose first: it is not an agent sent to act on the user's behalf, but the model through which she knows you, and a mirror in which the user looks back on themself: she uses it to anticipate more accurately how you would choose and react, and the user uses it to search and look back on their own lifetime of memory. The product discipline is the same as for the Behavioral Twin, only stricter: it is a personal model, not “copying the person over”, and even less a stand-in; the materials must keep this distinction clear. Delivered purely as software, with no biological procedures of any kind.
neuroTwinProd.cap: Users get a personal twin calibrated with their own neural data
neuroTwinProd.pass: The calibrated version significantly outperforms the behavioral version on the persona consistency scale, and its boundary labeling passes compliance review
neuroTwinProd.val: The product endpoint of the emulation branch; accumulates personalized material for the Gate of Emulated Awakening (without changing its fallback status)
neuroTwinProd.man: Axiom 4 (Monopoly) + the boundary set by Axiom 6: resembling you ≠ being you — the product sells the former; the ruling on ascension is left to the convergence gates.
neuroTwinProd.sci: Product layer. Basis for the discipline: research notes §2.4 “emulation ≠ reconstruction” — calibration improves the predictive power for behavior and neural responses and does not constitute any progress on the identity question; product claims must not overstep this, nor present it as an agent or stand-in acting on the user's behalf. Source: research notes §2.4
neuroTwinProd.open: Open question: the boundary of users' perception of the calibrated twin (once it is more like them, do users treat it as “another me”?) is an open product-ethics question, managed through boundary labeling and scale monitoring.
neuroTwinProd.unlock: The product endpoint of the emulation branch
neuroTwinProd.dur: Delivered after the convergence research meets its targets

replace.name: Gradual Replacement
replace.summary: A person's brain is gradually turned into silicon, step by step, while their first-person sense of self stays continuous.
tags: External dependency: a device that can replace a single neuron — does not exist today
Our research: continuity validation framework (see Memory as Continuity)
replace.body: The path proposed by Moravec (1988) and supported by Chalmers (2010) on the basis of organizational invariance: replace neurons one by one with silicon equivalents, with the person awake throughout, no interruption and no duplicate. Philosophically, this is the only route that directly answers “a copy is not the original person”, but no device exists today that can replace a single neuron — the device is an external breakthrough; the part we can advance is the validation framework of Memory as Continuity. It is an organizing principle that guides research, not an engineering project that can be scheduled. ⚠ Mutually exclusive: mutually exclusive with “Destructive Scan Emulation”. The two ascension mechanisms are an either-or choice for the same person: this node requires the original to persist throughout, with no interruption and no second claimant; Destructive Scan Emulation requires the original to die in the scan, with a copy being what runs — light up one, and the other is switched off. The mutual exclusion locks only these two points: all the other nodes leading to them are shared and do not exclude each other. This tree's ruling: this node is primary (Axiom 5, Axiom 6), and Destructive Scan Emulation is the fallback.
replace.cap: The person's substrate itself becomes silicon-based step by step, with first-person continuity of the self
replace.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Bidirectional Read/Write holding at single-neuron fidelity + a validated functional model of the neuron + the checkpoints of Memory as Continuity (all required)
replace.mode: External breakthrough (device) + our continuity validation research
replace.pass: First prove at the level of animal circuits: after a circuit is replaced, behavior and memory individuality are verifiably preserved
replace.val: Passes through the Gate of Gradual Replacement — the strongest identity status of the four gates
replace.man: Axiom 6 (Ascension), Manifesto V3.6.3 · Future of Ascension: "The transfer is gradual: the self moves over bit by bit, in one continuous movement." Axiom 5, Manifesto V3.6.3 · The Body and the Soul: "The body changes, the soul remains." Gradual replacement is the tree's preferred engineering counterpart of these two lines. the older quoted contrast "not a one-time copy" / "not copying over" is not found as wording in V3.6.3.
replace.sci: This is a line of thought with clear sources, not an existing technology: Hans Moravec, “Mind Children” (1988), proposed replacing neurons one by one with artificial devices while the person stays awake throughout; Sandberg & Bostrom, “Whole Brain Emulation: A Roadmap” (Oxford FHI Technical Report 2008-3), list it as an alternative route to destructive scanning; David Chalmers (2010), on the basis of organizational invariance, argues that the gradual route is more likely to preserve consciousness; Parfit (1984) holds that what matters is psychological continuity, not physical continuity. The honest ruling of the research notes: no device exists today that can replace a single neuron — it first requires bidirectional read/write at single-neuron fidelity plus a validated functional model of the neuron, and neither exists yet. Source: research notes §2.3
replace.open: Open question: single-neuron devices do not exist, and each of their prerequisites (single-neuron-fidelity read/write + a validated neuron model) is itself an open problem — this node has no date, only a direction.
replace.dur: No date — long-term research goal; the clock starts on the day the prerequisites hold at single-neuron fidelity

scan.name: Destructive Scan Emulation
scan.summary: An entire human brain is scanned and runs as an emulation on silicon, with the original destroyed in the process.
scan.when: After the lower bound in the literature
tags: External dependency: human brain scanning throughput of about 190,000 electron-microscope-years
scan.body: The two anchors given in the literature are presented side by side: the trend-extrapolation estimate (Igarashi/Ford, often misattributed as a conclusion of the State of Brain Emulation Report itself) puts human emulation after 2044; the academic median expectation (a survey of 312 neuroscientists, PLOS ONE 2025) says 2125. The two differ by about 80 years and both are predictions; they are presented side by side, without choosing one. The destructive scan route (preserve → section → reconstruct → run) additionally carries the identity problem: the original dies in the scan, and what runs is a copy. The “hard problem” of consciousness (Chalmers 1995) is not an engineering problem either. ⚠ Mutually exclusive: mutually exclusive with “Gradual Replacement”. An either-or choice for the same person: this node requires the original to die in the scan, with a copy being what runs; Gradual Replacement requires the original to persist throughout, with no interruption and no copy — light up one, and the other is switched off. The mutual exclusion locks only these two points; all the other nodes are shared. This tree's ruling: Gradual Replacement is primary, this node is the fallback.
scan.cap: A complete human brain running on silicon
scan.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Mouse-Scale Emulation + Personal Twin Convergence + the preserved-brain input provided by Readout (all required)
scan.mode: External breakthrough (industry-wide engineering); we only track it
scan.pass: First answer, at the mouse level, the testable question “does the emulation carry on the original individual's memory and behavioral individuality?”
scan.val: Passes through the Gate of Emulated Awakening — the weakest identity status, serving only as the fallback
scan.man: Axiom 6 (Ascension), Manifesto V3.6.3 · Future of Ascension: "The transfer is gradual: the self moves over bit by bit, in one continuous movement." The tree treats Destructive Scan Emulation as only a fallback gate. the older claim that the Manifesto itself wants "moving over, not copying over" as an explicit contrast is not found as wording in V3.6.3.
scan.sci: The two anchors differ by about 80 years and must be presented side by side with their sources kept distinct: ① trend extrapolation (Igarashi 2025 / Ford et al. 2024, cited via discussions related to the report) — extrapolating from technology trends to the feasibility of cell-level emulation: mouse around 2034, marmoset around 2044, human after 2044; it is not a direct finding of the State of Brain Emulation Report 2025 itself, nor does it describe an emulation that has been demonstrated; ② expert survey (PLOS ONE 2025-06-24, n=312) median years: nematode around 2045, mouse around 2065, human around 2125, with only a 10% probability that the first human whole-brain emulation appears before around 2075, and a bimodal distribution. One is trend extrapolation and the other expert judgment; both are predictions, not measurements — we do not average them or pick the one that sounds better. Scale gap: the human brain has about 86 billion neurons / about 150 trillion synapses, versus 139,000 / 54.5 million for the fruit fly; MICrONS's 120,000 neurons are only about 0.17% of the whole mouse brain (about 70 million neurons, about 500 mm³). The primary bottleneck identified by the report is scanning speed (per secondhand summaries, current rates are about 100,000 times too slow for a human brain), not compute. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §4; State of Brain Emulation Report 2025, arXiv:2510.15745; Zeleznikow-Johnston et al., PLOS ONE 2025
scan.open: Open question: the two literature anchors differ by nearly a century (after 2044 vs. a median of 2125); the questions of identity and consciousness are not engineering problems and will not disappear as scanning gets faster.
scan.dur: Trend-extrapolation estimate: after 2044; academic survey median: 2125 — different sources, about 80 years apart; both numbers are presented together, without choosing one

continuity.name: Memory as Continuity
continuity.summary: Personal continuity becomes something engineers can check step by step, using memory checkpoints instead of philosophical claims.
continuity.when: Long term · validated jointly with the ascension mechanisms
continuity.body: Our research: the devices come from outside; the validation framework comes from us. If the memory bridge holds, Gradual Replacement gains its most critical component: as each circuit is replaced, its memory function has already been mirrored and validated by an external system, and continuity has engineering checkpoints. Conversely, the companion's long-term memory model is also the validation model for Gradual Replacement: at each step of replacement, check against her model of the user — if she still recognizes you and you still recognize her, the replacement has not lost identity. The research covers checkpoints, criteria and procedures, all of it software and methods, involving no devices or biological experiments of any kind.
continuity.cap: Continuity turns from a philosophical claim into an engineering process with checkpoints
continuity.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Companion Memory Bridge + Bidirectional Read/Write + Memory Trust & Provenance Research + Long-term Persona Drift Monitoring Research (all required)
continuity.pass: Validated jointly with Gradual Replacement at the level of animal circuits (experiments run by external partners, criteria provided by us)
continuity.val: Passes through the Gate of the Memory Bridge, or, together with Gradual Replacement, through the Gate of Gradual Replacement
continuity.man: Axiom 5 (The Body and the Soul), Manifesto V3.6.3 · The Body and the Soul: "ascension means that humanity, while following AGI, remains itself." Whether identity is preserved is not declared by the Manifesto; it is checked item by item by her memory. the older wording "does not mean abandoning one's soul and consciousness" is not found as a sentence in V3.6.3.
continuity.sci: The positions have sources and their status is labeled: Parfit, “Reasons and Persons” (1984) — what matters is psychological continuity, not physical continuity; Chalmers (2010), organizational invariance — if causal organization is preserved, consciousness is preserved. These two are the philosophical foundation of this research, but the weight of the opposing side has been updated per the check: in the 2025 survey (n=312), scientists' median confidence that “long-term memories can be extracted from a static snapshot” was about 40%, and that “a whole-brain emulation can be built from a preserved brain” about 40% (62% when electrophysiological data recorded during life are available) — “memory carries continuity” is far from a consensus in the scientific community. This research is therefore a research program: break continuity down into memory checkpoints that can be checked item by item, and first validate them jointly with Gradual Replacement at the level of animal circuits, rather than announcing the conclusion first. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §4; Parfit 1984; Chalmers 2010; PLOS ONE 2025 survey
continuity.open: Open question: the completeness of the checkpoints cannot be guaranteed a priori — they can only be added item by item as animal-circuit validation proceeds; the framework itself is a living research program.
continuity.unlock: The continuity validation framework for the Gate of Gradual Replacement and the Gate of the Memory Bridge
continuity.dur: Long term; timed jointly with Gradual Replacement at the level of animal circuits

longevityExt.name: Longevity Medicine & Reprogramming (External Breakthrough)
longevityExt.summary: If outside researchers prove a longevity treatment works, the roadmap's overall timeline gets re-estimated; nothing more.
tags: We do not develop drugs or do biological research
This node does not grow a branch of our products
longevityExt.body: A purely external node — first, the boundary stated firmly: in this tree, longevity medicine only ever has external nodes. No “healthspan”-type node may carry “Our product” or “Our research”: we do not develop drugs, do not do wetware biological research, and do not do aging interventions. The state of the science is determined externally: no drug anywhere in the world has been approved to slow aging; what has real human outcomes is disease prevention (the GLP-1-class SELECT trial, HR 0.80); partial reprogramming (OSK), the approach with the highest ceiling, is still at the stage of first human dosing in an eye-disease indication (Life Biosciences ER-100, 2026-06), and is held back by aging biomarkers (ARPA-H PROSPR/VITAL-H is being built: 726 people, three already-marketed drugs vs. placebo, enrollment not starting until 2027, no results). The first human data from ER-100 must also be narrowed: it is only a 3-person, 56-day eye-disease safety observation (company-reported), not a longevity result. Lighting up this node means only this: if any external route is proven by regulators and science, the tree's overall time budget is rewritten — all we do is track and reassess; we do not build integration products, do not offer follow-up services, and do not make any efficacy claims.
longevityExt.cap: An externally established longevity breakthrough rewrites the whole tree's time budget (and nothing more)
longevityExt.mode: External breakthrough — driven by pharmaceutical companies, academia and regulators; we only track it
longevityExt.pass: Any route is approved for a single disease, or aging biomarkers are accepted as a surrogate endpoint
longevityExt.val: Unlocks none of our products or research; only affects the pricing of the preservation option and the assessment of the far end of the tree
longevityExt.man: Axiom 6 (Ascension), Manifesto V3.6.3 · Future of Ascension: "The question of longevity has always been asked wrong: how to make this body live a few more years. The real question is whether the self can outlive the body." So in this tree, longevity is only an external backdrop, not our business.
longevityExt.sci: Item by item, per the check's wording: SELECT (Lincoff et al., NEJM 2023, NCT03574597) n=17,604, aged ≥45, BMI ≥27, with established cardiovascular disease, without diabetes, semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly vs. placebo, mean follow-up 39.8 months, primary endpoint (cardiovascular death/non-fatal myocardial infarction/non-fatal stroke) 6.5% vs. 8.0%, HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90) — a 20% relative and 1.5-percentage-point absolute reduction; the FDA granted Wegovy a cardiovascular indication on 2024-03-08. It is a cardiovascular outcomes trial, not an aging/longevity trial, and does not demonstrate primary prevention, benefit in people without cardiovascular disease, or extended lifespan. Partial reprogramming ER-100 (Life Biosciences): received FDA IND clearance on 2026-01-28 (the first partial reprogramming therapy cleared for human trials), first patient dosed on 2026-06-09, Phase 1 NCT07290244, indications glaucoma + NAION (optic neuropathy), planning about 18 adults aged 40–85, a single intravitreal injection of OSK factors + oral doxycycline for about 8 weeks to switch it on, primary completion expected 2027-05; on 2026-10-08 the company reported first data at AAO/Eyecelerator: 3 patients with open-angle glaucoma, lowest dose 2×10¹¹ vg, followed to day 56, no dose-limiting toxicities/adverse events of special interest/serious adverse events, preliminary visual-field improvement in 2 patients, and the DSMB recommended escalating to 6×10¹¹ vg — company-reported, not peer-reviewed, open-label and uncontrolled, n=3, 56 days, and no epigenetic-age endpoint reported: it is an eye-disease safety trial, not a longevity result, and must not be described as “rejuvenation”. ARPA-H VITAL-H: announced 2026-02-24 (the PROSPR program totals $144 million across 7 teams), with the Barshop Institute receiving up to $38 million; 726 adults aged 60–65 randomized to rapamycin/dapagliflozin/semaglutide/placebo, followed for 3 years, with WHO intrinsic capacity as the healthspan endpoint — enrollment is expected to start in 2027; as of 2026-10-21 no ClinicalTrials.gov record was found, and there are no results of any kind. Background facts: as of 2026-10, the FDA does not recognize aging as an indication, and no anti-aging drug has been approved; TAME (metformin) was still waiting for launch funding as of mid-2026. All of this is other people's science; this node only tracks it. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §5; Lincoff et al., NEJM 2023 (SELECT); Life Biosciences ER-100 company report (2026-10-08); ARPA-H PROSPR / VITAL-H announcement (2026-02-24, EurekAlert)
longevityExt.open: Open question: ER-100 has only n=3, 56-day, open-label safety data, with no efficacy and no epigenetic-age endpoint, and primary completion is expected 2027-05; VITAL-H enrollment is not expected to start until 2027, with no registry record and no results. No human lifespan trial has been completed; every ranking rests on animal data or disease endpoints.
longevityExt.unlock: None — a purely external node; unlocks none of our products or research; only rewrites the assessment of the whole tree's time budget
longevityExt.dur: No fixed year; the trigger is any route being approved or a biomarker being accepted — and it only affects assessment, not our schedule

preserveSci.name: Brain Preservation Structural Fidelity (External Progress)
preserveSci.summary: Outside scientists create a measurable standard for how faithfully brain preservation keeps the brain's structure.
tags: We do not do preservation or build preservation facilities
preserveSci.body: A purely external node: preservation science is in other people's hands. Aldehyde-stabilized cryopreservation (ASC) has been shown in rabbits (2016) and whole pig brains (2018) to preserve connectome-level ultrastructure, winning the Brain Preservation Foundation's Large Mammal Prize; but fixation makes biological revival impossible, ASC is compatible only with future scan-and-emulate readout, and whether the preserved information is enough to reconstruct a person is an open empirical question. This node tracks external progress on fidelity assessment standards — once it lights up, the preservation option membership service has partners it can deliver with and a fidelity measure that can be checked.
preserveSci.cap: The structural fidelity of preservation gains a quantifiable external assessment measure
preserveSci.mode: External breakthrough — driven by preservation organizations and academia; we only track it
preserveSci.pass: A quantifiable third-party assessment standard appears for the information fidelity of preservation protocols
preserveSci.val: Unlocks the delivery-quality baseline of the ASC preservation option membership service
preserveSci.man: Axiom 6 (Ascension): first store “you” at the highest fidelity — the storage technology belongs to others; what we are responsible for is the arrangements and the archive.
preserveSci.sci: Structural preservation has prize-level evidence, and an equally important other side of qualifications: Aldehyde-stabilized cryopreservation (ASC) — McIntyre (now Aurelia Song) and Fahy, Cryobiology 2015 (glutaraldehyde perfusion to crosslink proteins + cryoprotectant, cooled to about –135 °C) — won the Brain Preservation Foundation's Small Mammal Prize in 2016-02 (whole rabbit brain, independent 3D electron microscopy assessment of synaptic connectivity preservation across the whole brain), and on 2018-03-13 won the Large Mammal Prize (whole pig brain, $80,000, prize pool $100,000, 21st Century Medicine, verified by 3D electron microscopy after rewarming). The qualifications that must be stated at the same time: the two prizes went to the same lab, the same method and the same judging committee; reviews as of 2026-09 show that no independent lab has replicated ASC at large-mammal scale; the foundation itself says a single demonstration is “insufficient to support the quality control that should accompany application to human patients”, and it does not endorse offering ASC or any preservation method to human patients. ASC preserves structure; chemically fixed tissue = biologically dead, not revival. Nectome's 2026-03 bioRxiv preprint on pig brain preservation is not peer-reviewed, and this page does not update its conclusions on that basis. Source: science check (2026-11-09) §5; Brain Preservation Foundation Large Mammal Prize announcement (2018-03-13); McIntyre & Fahy, Cryobiology 2015
preserveSci.open: Open question: ASC has not been replicated by any independent lab at large-mammal scale, and the foundation itself does not endorse offering it to humans; whether the preserved information is enough to reconstruct a person is an open empirical question; no third-party quantitative fidelity standard exists yet, and this node lights up when one appears.
preserveSci.unlock: The fidelity baseline for the Brain Preservation Option: ASC Archive (Membership Service)
preserveSci.dur: Completion criterion: a third-party fidelity assessment standard appears

preserve.name: Brain Preservation Option: ASC Archive (Membership Service)
preserve.summary: Members can arrange for partner organizations to preserve their brain, combined with their lifetime memory archive, as an option, not a promise of revival.
preserve.when: Contracts can be signed immediately (partnership layer)
tags: Our product: advance arrangement and archive integration service
Partners: preservation organizations perform the preservation
preserve.body: The product boundary, stated explicitly: our product is advance arrangements + integration with the lifetime memory archive — contract arrangements, archive merging, family procedures, long-term liaison; the preservation itself (perfusion, fixation, cold storage) is performed by partner organizations (organizations such as Alcor — whole body $220,000 / neuro only $80,000, about 250–263 preserved patients — are in operation); we do not build preservation facilities or perform preservation procedures. The other side must be stated at the same time: about 737 people worldwide are currently cryopreserved (secondhand figure), with only 30–40 added each year; no one has ever been revived, and no provider claims revival is possible today; preserved people are legally dead. What is sold is an option, not revival.
preserve.cap: “You” are archived at connectome-level fidelity (performed by partners), combined with your lifetime memory archive into one complete option
preserve.pre: [Multiple prerequisites · all required] Brain Preservation Structural Fidelity (External Progress) (fidelity measure) + Memory Export & Inheritance (lifetime archive) (all required)
preserve.mode: Partnership: we handle membership arrangements and archive integration; partners handle preservation
preserve.pass: The membership process and archive integration complete their first real deliveries, and the fidelity measure is checked against external standards
preserve.val: Unlocks Archive Integrity Assessment Research; the archive is the input to Readout
preserve.man: Axiom 6 (Ascension), Manifesto V3.6.3 · Future of Ascension: "whether the self can outlive the body" — the ASC preservation option is the only share of that question that can be bought today: an option, not a promise.
preserve.sci: Industry status per the range-based figures from the 2026 check (sources differ by 10–15 people, so ranges are used instead of single points): Alcor about 250–263 preserved patients (116 of them neuro-only, per the 2026-01 figure), about 1,500–1,535 members, whole body $220,000 / neuro only $80,000 (including standby); Cryonics Institute about 268–276 preserved patients (plus 279 pets), about 1,995–2,000 members, $28,000 (lifetime member)/$35,000/$45,000, whole body only, but standby/transport is paid separately (Suspended Animation typically $60,000–$78,000), for a real total cost of about $88,000–$128,000.
